text:
Marta: opening intake for a lightweight request-priority / queueing signal we can use at routing time. problem statement below, looking for gaps and owners.

Problem: noisy tenants and bursty workloads cause capacity contention. our current routing keys (model, region, tier) are too coarse — a single tenant can consume a disproportionate share and push others into higher latency or retries. customers keep asking for a way to express which tenant requests should be treated with higher scheduling preference during contention.

Proposal (alpha):
- Add an optional request field `request_priority` (0-10) and a per-tenant default.
- Routing layer uses `request_priority` as a soft signal: prefer higher-priority pools/variants and preempt best-effort queues when necessary.
- Provide Console + API controls to set tenant defaults + one-click toggle to make the field admin-only.
- Surface deterministic fallback reasons in traces (e.g., `fallback:pool_saturated->variant:gpu-q4`).

Goals:
- Minimal latency/throughput impact when not used.
- Pilot with 2 customers and validate reduced cross-tenant tail latency.
- UX: simple slider + cost tooltip for >7 priority.

Non-goals (phase 1):
- No per-tenant scaling policies or pricing changes.
- Not supporting arbitrary weight schedules or quotas in alpha.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Pilot tenants see >=40% reduction in p99 interference vs baseline under contested load.
- No increase in overall error rates >0.5% attributable to routing changes.
- 2 pilots live and integrated within 6 weeks.

Acceptance checklist (alpha):
- API accepts `request_priority` header/body field (int 0-10) and Console allows tenant default.
- Routing decision logs/traces include `priority_applied` boolean and `fallback_reason` tag.
- Admin-only toggle in Console implemented.
- E2E test simulating saturation and verifying preemption/fallback behavior.
- Runbook + rollback plan documented.

Notes / open questions:
- enforcement: should we honor priority across dedicated and private deployments the same way? (needs legal/enterprise input)
- cost callouts: high priority may increase unit cost if routed to faster pools — how explicit do we want to be in billing UI?

Marta: pinging for feedback and volunteers to own rollout checklist and telemetry. who can take ownership of the E2E test harness? :eyes:

Ajay: can we get tenant p95/p99 baseline for top 15 tenants? need that for the threshold modelling. I can take the measurement if infra gives me access.

Kevin: MarketplaceCo + ChatOps Inc would be good pilots. agree admin-only to start. I can intro PMs and legal contact. :+1:

Olivia: UX: mock attached in a follow-up DM. inline cost tooltip for >7 priority is important. also show a subtle banner in Console explaining "soft priority — does not guarantee absolute isolation".

Sam (eng): quick question on semantics — does priority force eviction of ongoing requests or only prefer scheduling for new requests? prefer new-requests-only for alpha. can we implement a short TTL for priority hints?

Priya (SRE): we'll need observability: per-tenant competing-queue metrics, `priority_applied` counters, and a saturation alert. I'll own dashboards if eng exposes the tags.

Nora (design): small wording nit — prefer "request priority" over "tenant priority" in UI to emphasize per-call override. otherwise looks good.

rollout-bot: created task RW-1892: implement routing signal and trace tags. assignees: unassigned.

Marta: thanks — volunteering list so far: Ajay (baseline metrics), Priya (dashboards/alerts), Kevin (pilot PM liaise), Sam (E2E harness), Olivia & Nora (Console + copy). I'll draft a minimal RFC after incorporating notes.
